title: RustConf 2017 - Closing Keynote: Safe Systems Software and the Future of Computing by Joe Duffy
summary: Joe Duffy's RustConf 2017 closing keynote on his experience at Microsoft building Midori, an operating system written in a Rust-like safe systems language. He covers the technical and cultural challenges of applying those lessons to Windows.
why: HN repeatedly cites it for Midori lessons: compatibility matters for adoption, and the Windows team stayed sceptical even with Midori running real workloads.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: I summarized this excellent talk here [1], but one of the main points is that compatibility with existing systems is important for adoption.
